sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里做DJ的时候，你每天晚上也要带着300张你最珍爱的藏品去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个像美丽的50年历史文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, Bill Cosby has been found guilty of sexual assault after years of claims against him.
sentences.zh: 今天，在经历多年的指控后，比尔· Cosby 被裁定性侵罪名成立。

sentences.en: What changed between the first trial and the second?
sentences.zh: 第一次庭审和第二次庭审之间发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: It's Friday, April 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月27日，星期五。

sentences.en: Hey, Graham, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，格雷厄姆，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: Call me one minute, Michael.
sentences.zh: 等我一分钟，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I'll call you back.
sentences.zh: 我一会儿打给你。

sentences.en: I'll call you one minute, please.
sentences.zh: 请等我一分钟再打给你。

sentences.en: Okay, bye.
sentences.zh: 好的，再见。

sentences.en: I called my colleague, Graham Bowley, on Thursday afternoon, right after the verdict had come down in the Cosby trial.
sentences.zh: 我在周四下午给我的同事格雷厄姆·鲍利打了个电话，就在科斯比案的裁决结果出来后不久。

sentences.en: Hey, Graham, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，格雷厄姆，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: Hi, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗨，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 那么。

sentences.en: It sounds like that was a little bit of a hectic scene.
sentences.zh: 听起来当时现场有点混乱。

sentences.en: It was an amazing scene for Mr. Cosby to come out, which he did.
sentences.zh: 对科斯比先生来说，走出来的那个场景太惊人了，他确实走了出来。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: He just walked out of the courtroom?
sentences.zh: 他就这么走出了法庭？

sentences.en: Well, he came out of the courtroom onto the steps in this bright sunlight, and it was like a carnival.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他从法庭走出来，站在艳阳高照的台阶上，那场面就像个狂欢节。

sentences.en: Bill Cosby, three words for you.
sentences.zh: 比尔·科斯比，送你三个字。

sentences.en: Guilty, guilty, guilty.
sentences.zh: 有罪，有罪，有罪。

sentences.en: The accusers were there, the media was there, public's there.
sentences.zh: 原告们在那里，媒体在那里，公众也在那里。

sentences.en: His lawyer's first, a big train of them.
sentences.zh: 他的律师走在最前面，浩浩荡荡的一群人。

sentences.en: And they go down the side of the courtroom, it's very loud, it's a huge hubbub.
sentences.zh: 他们顺着法庭旁边走过去，声音非常大，非常喧闹。

sentences.en: And Mr. Cosby walking very slowly, and he raises his left hand.
sentences.zh: 科斯比先生走得很慢，他举起了左手。

sentences.en: You know, people are actually shouting, you know, attacking him, but also, we got you, Bill.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们实际上在呐喊，你知道，攻击他，但也有人在喊，我们支持你，比尔。

sentences.en: You know, there's somebody shouting very loud, we got you, Bill, we got you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有人在大声喊，我们支持你，比尔，我们支持你。

sentences.en: And he was led slowly down the side, and he stopped, and he was so loud, you couldn't hear anything.
sentences.zh: 他被缓缓引导着从旁边走过，他停了下来，声音太大了，你什么也听不见。

sentences.en: He didn't speak.
sentences.zh: 他没有说话。

sentences.en: We are very disappointed by the verdict.
sentences.zh: 我们对这个裁决非常失望。

sentences.en: We don't think Mr. Cosby's guilty of anything, and the fight is not over.
sentences.zh: 我们认为科斯比先生没有犯任何罪，战斗还没有结束。

sentences.en: His lawyers tried to speak, but he couldn't hear anything.
sentences.zh: 他的律师试图发言，但什么也听不见。

sentences.en: It was so loud.
sentences.zh: 声音太大了。

sentences.en: And then into his car, and he's just driven off with lights flashing, and his arm raised.
sentences.zh: 然后他上了一辆车，在闪烁的警灯中绝尘而去，手臂还高高举着。

sentences.en: He's gone.
sentences.zh: 他走了。

sentences.en: Let's just take a step back, because we really just dove right in here.
sentences.zh: 让我们退一步想想，因为我们刚才确实直接切入正题了。

sentences.en: Where exactly are you?
sentences.zh: 你现在到底在哪里？

sentences.en: I am in Norristown.
sentences.zh: 我在诺里斯敦。

sentences.en: I spent the day in court, in the courtroom here in Norristown.
sentences.zh: 我在诺里斯敦的法庭度过了这一天。

sentences.en: Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州。

sentences.en: Well, Bill Cosby's second trial on sexual assault charges won't be like his first trial.
sentences.zh: 嗯，比尔·科斯比关于性侵指控的第二次审判将与他的第一次审判不同。

sentences.en: Well, a judge in the Bill Cosby case has ruled that five additional accusers will be able to testify in the upcoming retrial next month.
sentences.zh: 嗯，比尔·科斯比案的一名法官裁定，另外五名原告将能够在下个月即将到来的重审中出庭作证。

sentences.en: Cosby's first trial ended in a hung jury in June.
sentences.zh: 科斯比的第一次审判于6月以陪审团无法达成一致而告终。

sentences.en: Only one prior accuser was allowed to testify in that trial, along with the main accuser, Andrea
sentences.zh: 在那次审判中，除了主要原告安德烈亚之外，只有一名先前的原告获准作证

sentences.en: Constand.
sentences.zh: 康斯坦德。

sentences.en: The verdict was read in the first Cosby trial last year in 2017.
sentences.zh: 去年，即2017年，比尔·科斯比案的第一次审判宣读了裁决。

sentences.en: I recall feeling devastated and distraught and just totally disappointed in humanity.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时感到心碎、崩溃，对人类彻底失望。

sentences.en: That I said to myself, there's no way I can go back next year.
sentences.zh: 我对自己说，我绝对不可能在明年回去。

sentences.en: I mean, not only did I tell that to myself, I also told that to friends of mine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不仅是这么对自己说的，我还把这话告诉了我的朋友们。

sentences.en: There's no way that I'm going to possibly be able to endure going back.
sentences.zh: 我绝不可能承受得住再次回去的痛苦。

sentences.en: Lily Bernard is one of Bill Cosby's many accusers, whose statute of limitations had run out, but who attended both of the trials.
sentences.zh: 莉莉·伯纳德是比尔·科斯比的众多原告之一，她的追诉时效已经过期，但她出席了两次庭审。

sentences.en: And then I stepped back, I thought, I said, hey, look, the purpose for me going back is to support Andrea Constand and the other five survivors.
sentences.zh: 然后我退后一步，心想，嘿，看，我回去的目的是支持安德烈亚·康斯坦德和其他五位幸存者。

sentences.en: I have to stand strong for them.
sentences.zh: 我必须为他们坚强地站出来。

sentences.en: So I just prepared myself.
sentences.zh: 所以我做好了心理准备。

sentences.en: I was in these last eight or 10 months in between the trials.
sentences.zh: 在两次庭审之间的这最后八到十个月里。

sentences.en: I felt a bit of trepidation.
sentences.zh: 我感到有些忐忑不安。

sentences.en: But now, being in a courtroom with a rapist was difficult.
sentences.zh: 但现在，和强奸犯同处一个法庭是艰难的。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I felt empowered because when Bill Cosby, and often he did this during the day, passed by me with just inches, you know, I was really pleased in that my heart
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我又感到自己充满了力量，因为当比尔·科斯比——他白天经常这样做——从我身边经过，距离只有几英寸时，你知道，我真的很高兴，我的心

sentences.en: didn't quiver, you know, my breathing didn't become short.
sentences.zh: 没有颤抖，你知道，我的呼吸也没有变短。

sentences.en: When he passed by me, I looked at him with disdain and I looked at him as if he were disempowered.
sentences.zh: 当他从我身边经过时，我带着鄙视看着他，我看着他就好像他已经失去了权力一样。

sentences.en: So being with him, you know, just inches away from him where I could literally put my hand
sentences.zh: 所以和他在一起，你知道，离他只有几英寸远，我甚至可以伸出手

sentences.en: out and touch him and not feel my heart quicken and not begin to hyperventilate and be able to stand firm and not even feel afraid, for me, it was really empowering.
sentences.zh: 去触摸他，而我的心跳没有加速，没有开始过度换气，能够坚定地站着甚至不感到害怕，对我来说，这真的让我感到充满了力量。

sentences.en: And it was a real moment of healing, a healing towards me.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的疗愈时刻，是对我的一种疗愈。

sentences.en: But his odor.
sentences.zh: 但是他的气味。

sentences.en: Oh, shoot, I'm going to cry behind me in that courthouse.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，我在那个法院后面要哭了。

sentences.en: I smelled the tobacco.
sentences.zh: 我闻到了烟草味。

sentences.en: I smelled his sweat.
sentences.zh: 我闻到了他的汗水味。

sentences.en: I smelled his cologne.
sentences.zh: 我闻到了他的古龙水味。

sentences.en: And that took me right back because I remember the smell.
sentences.zh: 这一下子把我带回了过去，因为我还记得那个气味。

sentences.en: However, the fact that I could stand there unshaken was good.
sentences.zh: 然而，我能毫发无伤地站在那里，这很好。

sentences.en: And then regardless of the verdict, it's still a victory.
sentences.zh: 不管判决结果如何，这仍然是一场胜利。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we'd sat two weeks of testimony and arguments.
sentences.zh: 所以我们经历了两个星期的证词和辩论。

sentences.en: Arguments finished on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 辩论在周二结束。

sentences.en: And Wednesday morning, the jury started deliberating, 11 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 周三早上，陪审团开始审议，11点钟。

sentences.en: And then they had a few questions.
sentences.zh: 然后他们提出了几个问题。

sentences.en: We went back in.
sentences.zh: 我们重新进去了。

sentences.en: The evidence was replayed.
sentences.zh: 证据被重新播放了。

sentences.en: And then finally, at about one o'clock, we get the message that they've got a verdict.
sentences.zh: 最后，大约一点钟，我们得到了他们已经达成裁决的消息。

sentences.en: So we all crammed into the courthouse.
sentences.zh: 于是我们全都挤进了法院。

sentences.en: In the back were some of the other victims who had sat through the whole proceedings.
sentences.zh: 后面坐着一些旁听了整个审判过程的其他受害者。

sentences.en: Mr. Cosby at the front.
sentences.zh: 科斯比先生坐在前面。

sentences.en: Andrew Constant there with her lawyer.
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚·康斯坦德和她的律师也在那里。

sentences.en: And very quickly, the jury came in.
sentences.zh: 很快，陪审团进来了。

sentences.en: So I was actually expecting when the jury came out, I was actually expecting another hung jury.
sentences.zh: 所以当陪审团出来的时候，我其实预料到会有另一个陷入僵局的陪审团。

sentences.en: That's what happened last year.
sentences.zh: 去年就是这样的。

sentences.en: So, you know, several times the jury kept coming back and saying, your honor, we are deadlocked.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，陪审团好几次回来都说，法官大人，我们陷入僵局了。

sentences.en: And, you know, and so the judge would say, well, go back and deliberate.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，所以法官会说，好吧，回去继续审议。

sentences.en: It's your duty.
sentences.zh: 这是你们的职责。

sentences.en: Try to come up with a verdict.
sentences.zh: 试着达成一个裁决。

sentences.en: And so they did this several times last year.
sentences.zh: 所以他们去年这样做了好几次。

sentences.en: And juror number two told everybody he was guilty on three counts.
sentences.zh: 2号陪审员告诉所有人他在三项罪名上都有罪。

sentences.en: And Mr. Cosby sat very quietly.
sentences.zh: 科斯比先生静静地坐着。

sentences.en: The only noise was a very loud cheer from some of the women who say they were also abused by Mr. Cosby.
sentences.zh: 唯一的噪音是一些声称也遭到科斯比先生虐待的女性发出的非常大声的欢呼声。

sentences.en: People cheering at the back.
sentences.zh: 人们在后面欢呼。

sentences.en: And they went out quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们很快就出去了。

sentences.en: And you could just hear them in the back in the hallways of the court cheering.
sentences.zh: 你能听到他们在法院后面的走廊里欢呼。

sentences.en: And so the court was very quiet.
sentences.zh: 所以法庭非常安静。

sentences.en: Andrea sat very quietly and didn't celebrate.
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚静静地坐着，没有庆祝。

sentences.en: When that poor person stood up and proclaimed righteously and strongly and in a loud voice, guilty on three counts, I was in a state of shock.
sentences.zh: 当那个可怜的人站起来，正义、坚定、大声地宣告三项罪名成立时，我处于震惊状态。

sentences.en: I felt like a volcano of emotion had erupted within me, beginning at my gut and going up to my heart.
sentences.zh: 我觉得一股情感的火山在我体内爆发了，从我的胃部一直蔓延到心脏。

sentences.en: And I felt like an explosion of sobbing was literally coming out of me.
sentences.zh: 我感觉啜泣的爆发简直要夺腔而出。

sentences.en: And I had to literally put my hand over my mouth because I just felt like, you know, crying, but not crying in despair, but crying in really jubilation, crying in vindication,
sentences.zh: 我不得不 literalmente 用手捂住嘴，因为我只是觉得，你知道，想哭，但不是在绝望中哭泣，而是在真正的狂喜中哭泣，在平反中哭泣，

sentences.en: crying in relief.
sentences.zh: 在解脱中哭泣。

sentences.en: Yes, I was crying in relief.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在如释重负地哭泣。

sentences.en: I was crying in victory.
sentences.zh: 我在为胜利而哭泣。

sentences.en: I was crying in gratitude.
sentences.zh: 我在满怀感激地哭泣。

sentences.en: We were all crying.
sentences.zh: 我们都在哭泣。

sentences.en: The three of us caught the survivors in there.
sentences.zh: 我们三个在那里抓住了幸存者。

sentences.en: And so they escorted us out because we were just making too much sobbing noise.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把我们护送了出去，因为我们抽泣的声音实在太大了。

sentences.en: And I think there's video on CNN where you see us bursting out the wooden courtroom door into this white courthouse hallway.
sentences.zh: 我想CNN上有视频，你能看到我们冲出木制的法庭大门，来到这个白色的法院走廊。

sentences.en: And we are literally collapsed on this banister.
sentences.zh: 我们简直瘫倒在这个栏杆上。

sentences.en: And we are sobbing and sobbing, just these wailing with joy and vindication and gratitude and relief.
sentences.zh: 我们泣不成声，发出带着喜悦、平反、感激和解脱的悲号。

sentences.en: And we are just beside ourselves, really.
sentences.zh: 真的，我们简直无法自控。

sentences.en: We had no idea that inside the courtroom they were having this heated argument.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道法庭里面正在发生激烈的争论。

sentences.en: Then there was a big outburst when the district attorney fought for Mr. Cosby not to be released until sentencing.
sentences.zh: 然后，当地区检察官力争不让科斯比先生在宣判前被释放时，爆发了一场大争吵。

sentences.en: He wanted to keep him in detention.
sentences.zh: 他想把他扣押起来。

sentences.en: And Mr. Cosby, at that point, burst out very aggressively towards Mr. Steele, because he said he was a flight risk and he had a plane.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，科斯比先生对斯蒂尔先生非常愤怒地爆发了，因为他说他有潜逃风险，而且他有一架飞机。

sentences.en: And Mr. Cosby swore at Kevin Steele and said, no, you know, I don't have a plane.
sentences.zh: 科斯比先生对凯文·斯蒂尔爆粗口说，不，你知道，我没有飞机。

sentences.en: And he was immediately subdued by his lawyers, who surrounded him very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他立刻被迅速围上来的律师们制服了。

sentences.en: In front of everybody, Cosby swore and kind of physically got a little aggressive towards the...
sentences.zh: 在所有人面前，科斯比爆了粗口，并且对……态度有点身体上的攻击性

sentences.en: Absolutely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的，是的。

sentences.en: This is a very big moment of the trial, and this is the one big outburSt.
sentences.zh: 这是审判中非常大的一个时刻，也是唯一的一次大爆发。

sentences.en: Otherwise, for many days, he'd sat there very quietly in the front, leaning back in his chair, staring at the table, walking in and out with his cane and helped by...
sentences.zh: 除此之外，很多天里他一直静静地坐在前面，椅子往后靠，盯着桌子，拄着手杖进进出出，并在……的帮助下

sentences.en: What did Cosby actually say?
sentences.zh: 科斯比到底说了什么？

sentences.en: What were the words he used?
sentences.zh: 他用了什么词？

sentences.en: You are so like, don't have a plane.
sentences.zh: 你太像……根本没有飞机。

sentences.en: The first thought was like, where's Andrea?
sentences.zh: 第一个想法是，安德烈亚在哪里？

sentences.en: I want to hug her.
sentences.zh: 我想拥抱她。

sentences.en: I want to hug her.
sentences.zh: 我想拥抱她。

sentences.en: Because last year, at the end of the reading of the verdict, we were so distraught, and she was just standing strongly.
sentences.zh: 因为去年宣读裁决结束时，我们非常痛苦，而她只是坚定地站着。

sentences.en: So this time, I was hoping I could see Andrea, but the police were escorting off to the side of the halls.
sentences.zh: 所以这次，我希望我能见到安德烈亚，但警察正护送着我们往走廊的一侧走去。

sentences.en: We had to move or something, because maybe the defendant was coming.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不移开还是怎么的，因为可能被告要来了。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But we were all trying to catch our breath and wipe our tears away and breathe deeply and to be able to step outside and meet the gaggle of media without collapsing.
sentences.zh: 但我们都在努力喘口气，擦干眼泪，深深地呼吸，以便能够走出去迎接蜂拥而至的媒体而不至于瘫倒。

sentences.en: And so once we composed ourselves and wiped our tears, we stepped out into the sunlight.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我们平复了心情，擦干了眼泪，我们就走进了阳光里。

sentences.en: It was a bright, beautiful, sunny day.
sentences.zh: 那是一个明亮、美丽、晴朗的日子。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of hugging, a lot of crying, a lot of high-fives.
sentences.zh: 有很多拥抱，有很多哭泣，有很多击掌。

sentences.en: It was joyous.
sentences.zh: 太欢乐了。

sentences.en: ...waiting for the district attorney to come in and give, you know, his press conference.
sentences.zh: ……等待地区检察官进来举行，你知道，他的新闻发布会。

sentences.en: And Andrea Constant's going to be with him.
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚·康斯坦德将和他在一起。

sentences.en: I don't think she's going to speak, but she's going to stand by his side with her lawyer.
sentences.zh: 我想她不会发言，但她会和她的律师一起站在他身旁。

sentences.en: And the district attorney, Kevin Steard, is going to talk about his victory here today, which is a big victory for him.
sentences.zh: 地区检察官凯文·斯蒂尔将谈论他今天在这里的胜利，对他来说这是一场巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: Thank you all for being here in our grand jury room.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家来到我们的大陪审团房间。

sentences.en: Kevin Steele is a guy who has pursued this case.
sentences.zh: 凯文·斯蒂尔一直在追查这个案件。

sentences.en: What was revealed through this investigation was a man who had spent decades preying on women that he drugged and sexually assaulted,
sentences.zh: 通过这次调查揭露的是，这样一个男人：他数十年来一直在捕食那些被他下药并遭受性侵的女性，

sentences.en: and a man who had evaded this moment here today for far too long.
sentences.zh: 而这个男人逃避今天这一刻已经太久了。

sentences.en: He used his celebrity.
sentences.zh: 他利用了他的名气。

sentences.en: He used his wealth.
sentences.zh: 他利用了他的财富。

sentences.en: He used his network of supporters to help him conceal his crimes.
sentences.zh: 他利用他的支持者网络来帮助他掩盖罪行。

sentences.en: And now we really know today who was behind that act, who the real Bill Cosby was.
sentences.zh: 而今天我们终于真正看清了那个行为背后的面目，看清了真正的比尔·科斯比是谁。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, we were not scared to pursue power and money.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，我们并不害怕追求权力和金钱。

sentences.en: Mr. Cosby was a very powerful person.
sentences.zh: 科斯比先生是一个非常有权势的人。

sentences.en: He made the point that, you know, Mr. Cosby had had lawyers from four different law firms over these many years in which he'd pushed back.
sentences.zh: 他指出，在这些年来的抗争中，科斯比先生曾聘请过来自四家不同律所的律师。

sentences.en: So we hope that this case sends a strong message that the victims of these types of crimes can come forward and be heard on what happened to them.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们希望这个案件能发出一个强烈的信号：此类犯罪的受害者可以勇敢站出来，让人们听到他们的遭遇。

sentences.en: But, you know, the history is that back in 2005 when Andrea came forward, the prosecutor at the time didn't pursue the case.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，历史是这样的：早在2005年安德烈亚站出来时，当时的检察官并没有起诉此案。

sentences.en: On behalf of our office, we are sorry for what happened then, but we got a chance to make up for it.
sentences.zh: 我代表我们办公室，为当时发生的事情感到抱歉，但我们得到了弥补的机会。

sentences.en: And we hopefully have.
sentences.zh: 希望我们已经做到了。

sentences.en: We hopefully have.
sentences.zh: 希望我们已经做到了。

sentences.en: And I hope that people recognize that you got to show courage like this lady did.
sentences.zh: 我希望人们能认识到，你必须展现出像这位女士这样的勇气。

sentences.en: Like she showed courage.
sentences.zh: 就像她展现出的勇气一样。

sentences.en: She stepped up, she went forward and and and we got to the right result.
sentences.zh: 她挺身而出，勇往直前，然后我们得到了正确的结果。

sentences.en: And and she stayed through this.
sentences.zh: 而且她坚持走到了最后。

sentences.en: You know, she didn't she didn't have to start down this journey with us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她本来不必和我们一起踏上这段旅程。

sentences.en: She didn't have to come here for the first trial.
sentences.zh: 她本来不必来参加第一次审判。

sentences.en: She didn't have to come here for the second trial.
sentences.zh: 她本来不必来参加第二次审判。

sentences.en: But she did.
sentences.zh: 但她来了。

sentences.en: I don't know if you know this,
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否知道这一点，

sentences.en: but is this the is this the first criminal conviction for a well-known figure accused of sexual harassment or sexual assault since the Me Too movement essentially?
sentences.zh: 但自从“我也是”（Me Too）运动兴起以来，这是不是针对被指控性骚扰或性侵的名人的第一起刑事定罪？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Blew open.
sentences.zh: 彻底引爆了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's the first high profile trial since the Me Too movement started.
sentences.zh: 这是“我也是”运动开始以来受关注度最高的一次审判。

sentences.en: 14 years later,
sentences.zh: 14年过去了，

sentences.en: it may be easy to forget that she was that first courageous person that stood up in public to go to the authorities and say that Bill Cosby drugged and sexually assaulted her.
sentences.zh: 人们可能很容易忘记，她才是那个第一个勇敢地公开站出来、向当局指控比尔·科斯比对她下药并实施性侵的人。

sentences.en: Her courage, her resilience in the face of horrible and unfounded attacks upon her and her family has been so inspiring to all of us.
sentences.zh: 在面对针对她和她家人的可怕且毫无根据的攻击时，她的勇气和韧劲对我们所有人都是巨大的鼓舞。

sentences.en: Lily, there's been a lot of talk about the idea that the main difference between the last trial and this one is that the Me Too movement happened in between.
sentences.zh: 莉莉，有很多人在讨论这样一种观点：上一次审判与这一次的主要区别在于，这期间发生了“我也是”运动。

sentences.en: Do you think that that's true?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I think that what the Me Too movement has done is help every member in society to understand that it's perfectly normal for a rape victim to wait years to report or to confront or to hold accountable their perpetrators.
sentences.zh: 我认为“我也是”运动所做的事，是帮助社会中的每一个人去理解：强奸受害者花上几年时间才去报警、对质或追究加害者的责任，是完全正常的。

sentences.en: Or it's perfectly normal for a rape victim to go back to their rapist because, you know, nine times out of ten, their rapist is a beloved individual.
sentences.zh: 或者说，强奸受害者回到加害者身边也是完全正常的，因为你知道，十之八九，强奸受害者所爱的人就是他们的加害者。

sentences.en: And so what the Me Too movement has done is actually provided a foundation for jurists, for the average person,
sentences.zh: 因此，“我也是”运动实际上为法官、为普通人、

sentences.en: for a jury of peers to be able to understand behavior of rape victims, you know, and to not to not to not look at their going back to their perpetrator,
sentences.zh: 为由同龄人组成的陪审团提供了一个基础，让他们能够理解强奸受害者的行为，并且不去、不去、不去把他们回到加害者身边的行为，

sentences.en: to not look at their having given a gift to their perpetrator after he drugged and raped them as an indication of guilt.
sentences.zh: 以及在被加害者下药并强奸后送给加害者礼物这一举动，当作是有罪的迹象。

sentences.en: It is not because these are perfectly normal behavior of rape victiMs.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是，因为这些都是强奸受害者完全正常的行为。

sentences.en: I stand here in the spirit of Martin Luther King, who said that the arc of the moral universe is long, but today it has bent towards justice.
sentences.zh: 我站在这里，带着马丁·路德·金的精神，他说过，道德宇宙的弧线很长，但今天它向着正义弯曲了。

sentences.en: We are vindicated, we are validated, and we are now part of the tsunami of women's power and justice.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了平反，我们得到了证实，我们现在是女性力量与正义浪潮的一部分。

sentences.en: I spoke to one of the women after the last verdict who had accused Bill Cosby of sexually assaulting her, and I'm sure you've spoken to many of them.
sentences.zh: 在上一次判决后，我与其中一位指控比尔·科斯比性侵的女性交谈过，我确信你也和她们中的许多人交流过。

sentences.en: And they were so crushed after that last verdict.
sentences.zh: 那次判决后她们感到非常崩溃。

sentences.en: They felt like they had, in their minds, been robbed of justice, but also they felt that every other woman had been robbed of justice, too.
sentences.zh: 在她们看来，她们不仅被剥夺了正义，而且她们也觉得其他所有女性都被剥夺了正义。

sentences.en: And so I wonder how the reaction today feels in contrast to that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想知道，今天这种反应与那时相比有何不同？

sentences.en: You know, there are more than 50 people, women, came forward to accuse Mr. Cosby.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有50多个人、女性站出来指控科斯比先生。

sentences.en: Andrea Constance is the only single one that's gone to a criminal trial.
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚·康斯坦斯是唯一一个进入刑事审判的。

sentences.en: The others had come forward too late to even be considered.
sentences.zh: 其他人站出来得太晚，甚至连被考虑的资格都没有。

sentences.en: So they saw Andrea's case as sort of the one chance of vindication, and they didn't get it last time, and they were crushed.
sentences.zh: 因此，她们将安德烈亚的案件视为获得平反的唯一机会，但上次她们没有得到，所以她们心碎了。

sentences.en: They did get it this time, and they're jubilant.
sentences.zh: 这一次她们得到了，她们欢欣鼓舞。

sentences.en: Do you get the sense that these women feel as if this verdict, even though they might not have testified, that this was their verdict, too?
sentences.zh: 你有没有觉得，这些女性感觉这次判决——尽管她们可能没有出庭作证——这也是她们的判决？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Pushed back and shamed by the Cosby side, and some of them branded as liars.
sentences.zh: 她们遭到了科斯比阵营的反扑和羞辱，其中一些人还被污蔑为说谎者。

sentences.en: And, you know, in seeing them day in, day out, I see them, they're first in the court in the morning, they're last to leave at night.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，看着她们日复一日，我看到她们早上第一个到法院，晚上最后一个离开。

sentences.en: When I leave in the evening after reporting, you know, 8 o'clock at night, they've been on the steps lighting candles.
sentences.zh: 当我晚上采访完离开时，比如晚上8点，她们还一直在台阶上点蜡烛。

sentences.en: They've thrown everything into this.
sentences.zh: 她们把一切都投入到了这件事中。

sentences.en: Lily, what does this verdict mean for you personally?
sentences.zh: 莉莉，这个判决对你个人来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: Three guilty verdicts for me personally means just a victory, you know, a victory for humanity, really, is how I look upon it.
sentences.zh: 三项有罪判决对我个人而言仅仅意味着一场胜利，你知道的，在我看来，这真的是全人类的胜利。

sentences.en: I look upon this victory as a victory for humanity.
sentences.zh: 我认为这场胜利是全人类的胜利。

sentences.en: And it has not only restored my faith in humanity, but it has also, you know, I think, just made culture turn this tremendous corner towards believing women.
sentences.zh: 它不仅恢复了我对人类的信念，而且我认为，它也让文化朝着相信女性的方向转过了一个巨大的弯。

sentences.en: And that's really a beautiful thing.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一件美好的事。

sentences.en: The jury in the Cosby trial found Bill Cosby guilty of three counts of aggravated indecent assault against Andrea Constance.
sentences.zh: 科斯比案的陪审团裁定比尔·科斯比对安德烈亚·康斯坦斯犯下三项严重猥亵侵犯罪名成立。

sentences.en: The judge has not yet set a sentencing date, but each count carries a penalty of up to 10 years in a state prison.
sentences.zh: 法官尚未确定宣判日期，但每一项罪名最高可判处10年州立监狱监禁。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一个专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ时，你每天都要带着300件你最珍爱的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个充满生机的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了美丽的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 立即在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼（Audemars Piguet）的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域一些举足轻重的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收听。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: How much of your legal work was handled by Michael Cohen?
sentences.zh: 你的法律事务有多少是由迈克尔·科恩处理的？

sentences.en: Well, as a percentage of my overall legal work, a tiny, tiny little fraction.
sentences.zh: 嗯，占我整体法律业务的比例非常、非常小。

sentences.en: But Michael would represent me and represent me on some things.
sentences.zh: 但迈克尔确实代表我处理过一些事情。

sentences.en: He represents me like with this crazy Stormy Daniels deal.
sentences.zh: 他代表我处理了比如像斯托米·丹尼尔斯这笔疯狂的交易。

sentences.en: He represented me.
sentences.zh: 他代表过我。

sentences.en: And, you know, from what I see, he did absolutely nothing wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且，据我所知，他绝对没有做错任何事。

sentences.en: During a wide-ranging telephone interview with Fox and friends on Thursday morning,
sentences.zh: 周四上午，在接受福克斯“朋友与早安”节目广泛的电话采访时，

sentences.en: President Trump acknowledged for the first time that his longtime lawyer, Michael Cohen, had represented him in efforts to silence Stephanie Clifford, the adult film actress,
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统首次承认，他的长期律师迈克尔·科恩曾代表他努力让斯蒂芬妮·克利福德保持沉默。斯蒂芬妮是一名成人电影女演员，

sentences.en: who said she had an affair with Trump a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 她曾声称自己在十年前与特朗普有过一段婚外情。

sentences.en: Trump had previously denied any knowledge of the $130,000 payment by Cohen to keep Daniels quiet, a payment that is now the subject of a federal investigation.
sentences.zh: 特朗普此前曾否认知道科恩为让丹尼尔斯闭口而支付的13万美元，这笔付款目前是联邦调查的对象。

sentences.en: Another gift from the heavens in this case.
sentences.zh: 这是本案中来自天堂的又一份大礼。

sentences.en: They keep coming.
sentences.zh: 这样的礼物接踵而至。

sentences.en: I don't know how I've fallen into such good luck in this case, but I'm going to take it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道在这个案子里我怎么会运气这么好，但我全盘接受。

sentences.en: Shortly after the Fox interview, Clifford's lawyer, Michael Avenatti, was asked about the president's disclosure on MSNBC's Morning Joe.
sentences.zh: 在福克斯采访后不久，克利福德的律师迈克尔·阿文纳蒂在 MSNBC 的《早安乔》节目中被问及总统的这一披露。

sentences.en: What's the impact of that?
sentences.zh: 这有什么影响？

sentences.en: It's a hugely damaging admission by the president, because according to what he said on Air Force One a few weeks ago, he didn't know anything about the agreement.
sentences.zh: 这是总统做出的极具破坏性的供认，因为根据他几周前在空军一号上的说法，他对这个协议一无所知。

sentences.en: He didn't know anything about the payment.
sentences.zh: 他对这笔付款一无所知。

sentences.en: Michael Cohen went off and did this on a lark, and Mr. Trump knew nothing about it.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·科恩是一时兴起去做了这件事，而特朗普先生对此完全不知情。

sentences.en: We now find out that that's bogus.
sentences.zh: 我们现在发现那是假的。

sentences.en: And on Friday, Kim Jong-un became the first North Korean leader to set foot in South Korean-controlled territory.
sentences.zh: 周五，金正恩成为第一位踏上韩国控制领土的朝鲜领导人。

sentences.en: In a dramatic start to a historic summit with South Korean President Moon Jae-in,
sentences.zh: 在与韩国总统文在寅历史性峰会的戏剧性开局中，

sentences.en: Kim walked from North Korea into the demilitarized zone which separates the North and South, and entered the peace house on the South Korean side.
sentences.zh: 金正恩从朝鲜步行穿过分隔南北的非军事区，进入了韩方一侧的和平之家。

sentences.en: In a major breakthrough, the two men agreed to work to remove all nuclear weapons from the Korean Peninsula and pursue a broader peace agreement that would end decades of conflict.
sentences.zh: 在一项重大突破中，双方同意致力于消除朝鲜半岛上的所有核武器，并寻求一项旨在结束长达数十年冲突的更广泛和平协议。

sentences.en: Both goals require the approval of the U.S., a major military ally of the South.
sentences.zh: 这两个目标都需要得到美国（韩国的主要军事盟友）的批准。

sentences.en: The summit sets the stage for a critical meeting between Kim and President Trump, scheduled for the coming weeks.
sentences.zh: 此次峰会为金正恩与特朗普总统定于未来几周举行的关键会晤奠定了基础。

sentences.en: The Daily is produced by Theo Belcom, Lindsay Garrison, Rachel Quester, Annie Brown, Andy Mills,
sentences.zh: 《每日播客》由西奥·贝尔科姆、林赛·加里森、雷切尔·克斯特、安妮·布朗、安迪·米尔斯、

sentences.en: Ike Srees-Khanaraja, Claire Tennisgetter, Paige Cowett, Michael Simon-Johnson, and Jessica Chung, with editing help from Larissa Anderson.
sentences.zh: 艾克·斯里斯-卡纳拉贾、克莱尔·坦尼斯盖特、佩奇·科维特、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊和杰西卡·钟制作，拉里萨·安德森提供剪辑协助。

sentences.en: Lisa Tobin is our executive producer.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·托宾是我们的执行制片人。

sentences.en: Samantha Hennig is our editorial director.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎·亨尼格是我们的编辑总监。

sentences.en: Our technical manager is Brad Fisher, and our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的技术经理是布拉德·费舍尔，主题音乐由奇迹乐队（Wonderly）的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯堡创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Sam Dolnick, Michaela Bouchard, Chris Wood, and Stella Tan.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢萨姆·多尔尼克、米凯拉·布沙尔、克里斯·伍德和斯特拉·陈。

sentences.en: And Juniper Claire Ratliff, welcome to the world.
sentences.zh: 还有朱尼帕·克莱尔·拉特利夫，欢迎来到这个世界。
zh_words: 朱尼帕·克莱尔·拉特利夫

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日播客》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: A reminder that tomorrow will bring you the second chapter of our new series, Caliphate, right here on The Daily.
sentences.zh: 提醒大家，明天我们将为您带来新系列《哈里发国》的第二章，就在《每日播客》。

sentences.en: See you Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个控制严密的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎进了一群自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又令人兴奋的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》中，我和萨拉·科尼格将带您聆听那些试图维持影响力却在过程中失控的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在您获取播客的任何地方订阅收听。
